title: Report progress to a board or steering group
summary: Steering groups need a clear, honest picture of progress, risks and decisions needed. Good reporting builds trust and gets you help when you need it.

beginner: Find out what the group wants to know and how often.
Lead with a one-line summary: on track, at risk or off track, and why.
Show progress against milestones and outcomes.
List the top risks and any decisions you need from the group.
Keep it to one page and be honest about problems.
intermediate: Lead with status and decisions needed.
experienced: Shape reporting around outcomes rather than activity.
Use the group to unblock problems.
Pre-brief the chair on difficult news.

toolExamples.power-bi: Use a one-page dashboard for the steering group.
toolExamples.confluence: Publish the report where members can read it before the meeting.

definitionOfDone: One-page report with status, progress, risks and decisions
pitfalls: Everything always shown as on track

sources.title: A product manager's guide to release planning (Atlassian)
